statements.label: supported
statements.text: Targeted therapies routinely given for lung cancer induce the cytidine deaminase A3A, producing ongoing mutagenesis in drug-tolerant cancer cells that survive treatment.
statements.evidence: lung cancer targeted therapies commonly used in the clinic can induce cytidine deaminase APOBEC3A (A3A), leading to sustained mutagenesis in drug-tolerant cancer cells persisting during therapy
statements.note: The abstract reports that clinically used lung cancer targeted therapies induce A3A and cause sustained mutagenesis in drug-tolerant cells persisting during therapy.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumours from patients with lung cancer who progressed after extended responses to targeted therapies were enriched for APOBEC mutational signatures.
statements.evidence: APOBEC mutational signatures are enriched in tumours from patients with lung cancer who progressed after extended responses to targeted therapies.
statements.note: The abstract states that APOBEC mutational signatures are enriched in tumours of patients who progressed after extended responses to targeted therapies.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Targeted therapies induce A3A in breast cancer cells in the same way they do in lung cancer cells.
statements.evidence: Here we report that lung cancer targeted therapies commonly used in the clinic can induce cytidine deaminase APOBEC3A (A3A)
statements.note: The abstract reports A3A induction only for lung cancer targeted therapies and says nothing about whether the same happens in breast cancer.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A3A induced by therapy drives double-strand DNA break formation and thereby raises genomic instability in drug-tolerant persister cells.
statements.evidence: Therapy-induced A3A promotes the formation of double-strand DNA breaks, increasing genomic instability in drug-tolerant persisters.
statements.note: The abstract reports that therapy-induced A3A promotes double-strand DNA breaks and increases genomic instability in drug-tolerant persisters.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose tumours underwent whole-genome sequencing in the programme survived longer than patients who received only standard-of-care genetic testing.
statements.evidence: The linkage of WGS and longitudinal life course clinical data allowed the assessment of treatment outcomes for patients stratified according to pangenomic markers.
statements.note: The abstract reports that outcomes could be assessed for patients stratified by pangenomic markers, but it never compares sequenced with unsequenced patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In glioblastoma multiforme, small variants turned up in 94% of cases and copy number aberrations affecting one or several genes in 58% of cases.
statements.evidence: in glioblastoma multiforme, small variants were present in 94% of cases and copy number aberrations in at least one gene in 58% of cases
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly these two frequencies for glioblastoma multiforme: 94% with small variants and 58% with copy number aberrations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Homologous recombination deficiency occurred in 40% of high-grade serous ovarian cancer cases, and 30% of these traced to pathogenic germline variants.

statements.note: The abstract reports homologous recombination deficiency in 40% of high-grade serous ovarian cancers, with 30% linked to pathogenic germline variants.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of the cancer types examined, sarcoma showed the highest frequency of actionable structural variants, at 13% of cases.
statements.evidence: sarcoma demonstrated the highest occurrence of actionable structural variants (13%)
statements.note: The abstract states that sarcoma had the highest occurrence of actionable structural variants, at 13%.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study pinpointed the helicase-encoding gene WRN on chromosome 8p as a haploinsufficient tumour-suppressor gene, backed by several independent lines of evidence.

statements.note: The abstract reports that BISCUT identified WRN on chromosome 8p as a haploinsufficient tumour-suppressor gene supported by several lines of evidence.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The loci that the method flagged were significantly enriched for known cancer driver genes, among them genes that analysis of focal copy-number events missed.
statements.evidence: These loci were significantly enriched for known cancer driver genes, including genes not detected through analysis of focal copy-number events, and were often lineage specific.
statements.note: The abstract reports significant enrichment of known cancer driver genes among these loci, including genes focal copy-number analysis did not detect.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.note: The abstract concerns the forces driving aneuploidy and its role in tumorigenesis, and reports nothing about treatment response.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rates of arm-level copy-number alterations correlated most strongly with the effects those alterations have on cellular fitness.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Loss of function in TP53, SMARCA4 and CDKN2A went together with a site-specific shorter interval to metastasis.

statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Live-cell imaging showed acentric fragments staying clustered in close spatial proximity throughout mitosis, so that one daughter cell inherited them asymmetrically.

statements.label: supported

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Depleting the CIP2A-TOPBP1 complex lowers how often micronuclei form in dividing cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inactivating the CIP2A-TOPBP1 complex scattered acentric fragments through the mitotic cytoplasm, so they partitioned stochastically into both daughter nuclei and built up as cytoplasmic DNA.
statements.evidence: Inactivation of CIP2A-TOPBP1 caused acentric fragments to disperse throughout the mitotic cytoplasm, stochastically partition into the nucleus of both daughter cells and aberrantly misaccumulate as cytoplasmic DNA.
statements.note: The abstract reports that inactivating CIP2A-TOPBP1 dispersed acentric fragments, which then partitioned into both daughter nuclei and misaccumulated as cytoplasmic DNA.
